newsitem.title: USA: Doubletree to acquire Red Lion.
newsitem.headline: Doubletree to acquire Red Lion.

text.p: Doubletree Corp and Red Lion Hotels Inc said they have signed an agreement under which Doubletree will acquire Red Lion in a deal worth $1.20 billion.
The deal will include Doubletree's acquisition of $200 million of Red Lion debt, the companies said.
Red Lion holders will recieve $30.11 per share, consisting of $21.20 cash and $8.81 worth (0.2398 share) of Doubletree common stock.

The companies said holders representing 67 percent of Red Lion's common shares, including a partnership of Red Lion co-founder Tod McClaskey, the pension funds of the states of Washington and Oregon and Kohlberg, Kravis Roberts and Co, have committed their support for the deal.
Most of Red Lion's locations will operate under the Doubletree name following the transaction, the companies said.

Doubletree said it has recieved written committments for financing the entire transaction. The deal will include Doubletree's issuance of $380 million in common stock and $600 million of institutional debt. The balance will be funded by an additional equity offering.
Tke McClaskey partnership will own about 13 percent of the new company and hold two seats on its board, the companies said.
Units of Red Lion Inns Master Limited Partnership, are not part of the transaction.
The deal is subject to approval by both companies' shareholders.
